To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the security index of actuators in networked control systems can be computed and used to protect vulnerable actuators, (ii) the security index can be increased by placing sensors, (iii) the robust index can characterize the vulnerability of actuators, can be computed in a tractable manner, and can be increased by sensor placement, and (iv) the robust index is related to the limited model knowledge attackers may have.

(1) the security index of a single actuator is the minimum number of actuators and sensors that must be compromised to conduct a perfectly undetectible attack against the actuator; (2) the index is NP-hard and can be sensitive with respect to variations in the system model; (3) a robust security index, based on limited model knowledge attackers, can be computed in a polynomial time and can be increased by placing sensors.
